<thought>Based on the data: C10H13NO2, DBE = 5, one carbonyl (166 ppm), six aromatic carbons (~129 ppm), and three aliphatic carbons (52, 43, 38 ppm). The aromatic region suggests a monosubstituted benzene ring. The aliphatic shifts are consistent with a –CH2–CH2–CH3 chain attached to the carbonyl (52 ppm for a carbon attached to N, 43 ppm for a carbon α to carbonyl, 38 ppm for a terminal methyl). This matches the structure of N‑ethyl‑benzamide (C6H5‑C(=O)‑NH‑CH2‑CH3). The fragments that can be joined to give the full molecule are the benzoyl fragment and the ethyl‑amine fragment. Their SMILES are: “c1ccccc1C(=O)” (benzoyl) and “NCC” (ethyl‑amine). Joining the N of the second fragment to the carbonyl carbon of the first yields N‑ethyl‑benzamide, which fits the molecular formula and NMR data.> 
<final_answer>['c1ccccc1C(=O)', 'NCC']</final_answer>
